user_request: Fix 39 test failures that appear when the Shepherd suite runs on macOS (built and verified on Linux as root). Three causes: (1) src/shepherd/host/mac.py MAC_DISPATCH_REQUIREMENTS=('timeout','nc') is wrong - macOS has no timeout binary, so hook dispatch is available=False and the signal engine would receive nothing; (2) tests/signals/conftest.py os.chown(path,65534,65534) is root-only and raises PermissionError for a normal macOS user; (3) macOS TMPDIR makes pytest tmp_path exceed the AF_UNIX sun_path budget (real macOS limit is 104, not Linux's 107).

intent.goal: The default pytest lane is green on macOS with no product behaviour lost, and hook dispatch actually works on this host.
non_goals: Weakening or deleting any existing assertion
Running the live lane as part of this fix

MAC_SOCKET_PATH_BUDGET reflects the real macOS sun_path limit, evidenced by a measurement on this host

investigator.root_cause: Product and tests both asked the Linux driver about a macOS host: MacHost.environ defaulted to {} (blind to HOME/TMPDIR), MacHost.hook_dispatch() refused unconditionally over an unmeasured netcat flag set, and eight test modules spelled LinuxHost() where they meant 'this host'.

critical_issues.title: The wedged-peer guard cannot fail - the listener it wedges against is not wedged
critical_issues.evidence: `conn` is a local; on return the frame dies, refcount hits zero, CPython closes the fd, so the 'accepts and never reads' peer hangs up immediately. Test runs in 0.02s vs the probe's own 264-324ms. Reviewer drove the test's Listener/dispatch by import with a command having NO outer bound: both assertions passed (code=0, elapsed=0.030s).
critical_issues.why: This is the single executable proof behind the D55 re-decision and acceptance criterion 6. Delete the perl/Time::HiRes wrapper and the suite stays green.
critical_issues.fix: Hold the accepted connection for the listener's lifetime (keep.append(conn)); add a negative control proving the fixture can produce the slow case.

findings.title: Age-only temp retention with no count cap
findings.evidence: du -sh /private/tmp/shp-501 -> 2.8G across 155 run dirs created today; largest base 218MB/1810 entries. RUN_RETENTION_S=24h is the only bound.
findings.fix: Union: never delete a base younger than a short grace window, AND keep only newest N by mtime beyond it.

findings.title: /tmp/shp-<uid> accepted regardless of owner or mode
findings.evidence: mkdir(mode=0o700, exist_ok=True) silently accepts a pre-existing dir; os.access(W_OK) returns True for root regardless. Tree runs as root on Linux, so a local user pre-creating /tmp/shp-0 gets a dir root then populates and prunes inside.
findings.fix: lstat the root; require st_uid==os.getuid() and st_mode & 0o077 == 0; else return None (already handled as 'leave pytest default alone').

findings.title: startswith('/usr/bin/') asserts PATH order, not stock-macOS presence
findings.evidence: A Homebrew perl or netcat puts /opt/homebrew/bin first and reds this test on a host where hook_dispatch() is correct.
findings.fix: Assert Path('/usr/bin/perl').is_file() for the stock claim and shutil.which(req) is not None for reachability - two different facts.

findings.title: One node id, two meanings: 40ms is a ceiling on macOS, a discriminator on Linux
findings.fix: macOS-only companion assertion that still discriminates, or accept explicitly as deferred.

open_observations: tests/conftest.py pytest_configure is NOT platform-gated: on Linux it relocates --basetemp from /tmp/pytest-of-root/pytest-N to /tmp/shp-0/<mkdtemp>, and pytest_sessionfinish deletes a GREEN run's base where pytest kept the last three. Test-harness behaviour only, not product - but it is the one change Linux will actually feel, against a stated non-goal.

Three sites still carry a silent pytest.skip('no dispatcher on this host'): if /usr/bin/perl or /usr/bin/nc vanished, 28 hook-lane tests would disappear without a red. The new test_hook_dispatch_delivery.py::entry_command asserts available is True rather than skipping, so the lane has one tripwire that cannot be skipped past.
